drafts.text:
Google just updated the wording on its payment processing times help page, and it matters today because it is Black Friday.

If your Google Ads account is on prepay, the page now lists Toss (previously LGU+) and says those payments should land within 3 business days, not the same afternoon. Bank debit is up to 5 business days. A money transfer is typically 5, and in some cases up to 30.

Three things to do before the day gets away from you:
1) Open Billing summary and check the payment method, pending payments, and remaining balance.
2) If you rely on Toss, bank transfer, or money transfer, have a credit card ready as backup, or confirm the balance already covers peak spend.
3) If a payment is past the window on that page, contact support with proof of payment.

PPC Times flagged the help-page change today. I opened the official page (answer/9436113). I have not seen the previous version, so I am not treating the old 24-hour wording as Google's own comparison.

drafts.text:
Most people will spend Black Friday trying to get their own product page cited by ChatGPT or Google AI. Last year's data says that is the wrong place to look.

iPullRank tracked hundreds of shopping prompts through Black Friday week 2025. In toy-related answers, publisher best-of lists rose from 46% to 65% of the links. Superstore questions went from 62% to 78%. Brand websites did not get a lift, and the brands named barely moved. The study does not show an effect on clicks or sales, and the 2026 data is due after Cyber Monday.

The 30-minute job today is simpler: ask the same "best Black Friday deals" queries your category actually uses, write down which listicles the answers link to, and check whether those pages still have your live price and in-stock link.

I am not reading that as a trading signal. I am reading it next to the Google Ads billing window: if you top up with a bank transfer that can take several business days, do not assume a same-day credit will be there to catch a Friday traffic spike.
